name: Indus Valley Civilization (Harappan)
summary: Spanning over 1,000 cities and towns across the Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra basins, Harappan cities featured rectilinear grid planning, indoor flush toilets, covered brick sewage drains, standardized binary-decimal weights, the Great Bath, and the world’s earliest tidal dockyard at Lothal.
keyFacts: World’s earliest municipal sanitation, covered sewers, and household bathrooms
Uniform fired-brick ratios (4:2:1) and ultra-accurate chert weight standards across 1,000+ km
Tidal dockyard at Lothal & undeciphered Indus script steatite seals

name: Vedic Period & Kuru-Panchala
summary: Period of the composition of the four Vedas (Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda), Brahmanas, and early Upanishads in Vedic Sanskrit, alongside iron-plow expansion across the fertile Gangetic plains.
keyFacts: Composition & oral preservation of the Rigveda and Upanishadic philosophy
Shulba Sutras geometry & Panini’s Ashtadhyayi (formal generative grammar of Sanskrit)

name: Sixteen Mahajanapadas & Magadha
summary: Second urbanization of India featuring 16 great states (including the Vajji/Licchavi republic at Vaishali), punch-marked silver coinage, Wootz crucible steel, and the birth of Buddhism and Jainism.
keyFacts: Birth of Buddhism (Siddhartha Gautama) and Jainism (Mahavira)
Gana-Sangha parliamentary assemblies at Vaishali & Wootz steel metallurgy

name: Maurya Empire → Kushan & Satavahana
summary: Founded by Chandragupta Maurya and unified from Afghanistan to southern India under Ashoka the Great. Shocked by the carnage of the Kalinga War (261 BCE), Ashoka renounced conquest, erected rock and pillar edicts promoting religious tolerance, wildlife hospitals, and social welfare, and sent Buddhist missions across Eurasia.
keyFacts: Edicts of Ashoka on polished sandstone pillars (Lion Capital of Ashoka is India’s national emblem)
Kautilya’s Arthashastra treatise on statecraft and economics
Grand Trunk Road (Uttarapatha) & Gandharan-Mathura Buddhist art under the Kushans

name: Gupta Empire & Chola Dynasty
summary: The Gupta Golden Age formalized the base-10 decimal place-value system with zero (0–9, modern "Hindu-Arabic" numerals), Aryabhata’s trigonometry and Earth-rotation astronomy, Nalanda University, Kalidasa’s Sanskrit drama, and the rust-proof Iron Pillar of Delhi, while the southern Chola Dynasty built Brihadisvara Temple and projected naval power across Southeast Asia.
keyFacts: Decimal place-value numeral system (1–9 and 0), trigonometry (sine/cosine), and Aryabhata’s astronomy
Nalanda Mahavihara residential university (10,000 students & 9-story library)
Ajanta Caves, rust-resistant Iron Pillar of Delhi, and Chola bronzes/Brihadisvara Temple

name: Delhi Sultanate, Vijayanagara & Mughal Empire
summary: Synthesizing Indo-Persian and indigenous traditions, the Mughal Empire under Akbar practiced universal religious tolerance (Sulh-i-Kul), built the Taj Mahal and Red Fort, and generated roughly a quarter of the world’s manufacturing output (cotton textiles, steel, spices) by 1700.
keyFacts: Taj Mahal, Fatehpur Sikri, Humayun’s Tomb, and Vijayanagara’s stone chariot at Hampi
Akbar’s Ibadat Khana interfaith dialogues & Todar Mal’s land revenue survey

name: Republic of India & South Asia
summary: Achieved independence in 1947 following Mahatma Gandhi’s non-violent Satyagraha campaign, adopting a secular democratic constitution with universal adult suffrage and growing into a major spacefaring (ISRO Chandrayaan-3 / Mangalyaan), digital, and economic power.
keyFacts: Non-violent independence movement inspiring global civil rights
World’s largest democratic elections, Green Revolution, and ISRO lunar/Martian missions
